title: synthetic-traffic-canary-stress-profiles-wip
body:
Purpose:
Build a small, portable cookbook for generating reproducible synthetic traffic for canary and A/B rollouts of LLM-powered routes. This is explicitly intended to complement production shadow traffic and to exercise edge-case load/behavior that real user traffic might not hit during short canaries (e.g., long-context chains, memory-heavy KV usage, rare token sequences).

Scope / when to use this:
- For staged releases where we need an accelerated signal for cost/latency regressions during the first 1–10% exposure windows.
- When evaluating fallback/failover configurations across model variants (quantized vs full float).
- Preflight run before an extended canary (to reduce surprise incident noise).
- Stress-profiling route-level autoscaling and batching heuristics.

Key goals:
- Produce deterministic synthetic workloads that map to realistic behavior: sequence-length distribution, prefix reuse, chat-turn patterns, function calling, and embedding-heavy bursts.
- Provide a small matrix of stress profiles (latency, throughput, hallucination-probe, memory-churn, token-burst).
- Define pass/fail thresholds that are actionable by oncall + product owners.
- Ensure low/no PII — synthetic payloads only.

Stress profile catalog (starter):
1) baseline-peak: 1x–2x observed 95p RPS for the route; short sequences (<=128 tokens); used to validate autoscaling triggers.
2) long-context-sweep: single-request sequences 2k–8k tokens; high KV cache warm-up. Measures p95/p99 latency and mem blowouts.
3) conversational-bursts: 10–30 turn simulated dialogs with back-and-forth references; validates KV reuse and prefix caching.
4) embedding-batch-blast: large embedding batched requests (batch sizes 64/128/256) to exercise batching and GPU memory.
5) hallucination-probe: adversarial prompts designed to solicit factual hallucinations and guardrail triggers; paired with evals harness to measure drift.
6) mixed-slo-mixer: hybrid traffic mixing low-latency short queries (high priority) and background long-generation jobs (low priority) to detect cross-traffic interference.

Representative metrics to capture (observability contract):
- infra: GPU util, memory usage, p95/p99 latency (generation), qps, tokens/s served, batching efficiency (tokens per kernel call)
- service: 5xx rate, retry rate, queue length, request timeout count, cold-starts
- model-quality: hallucination-rate (via eval harness), BLEU/ROUGE-ish proxies for structured outputs, embedding-cosine-drift vs baseline corpus
- cost: estimated $/k tokens at current routing, and variance under stress

Pass/fail heuristics (examples):
- p95 latency > baseline p95 * 2 for two consecutive 5-min buckets — FAIL (auto-pause canary if enabled)
- GPU OOM or infra-reported fatal memory threshold — FAIL (immediate stop)
- hallucination-rate increase > 15% vs pre-canary reference on same prompt-set — WARN -> human review
- 5xx increase > 0.5 percentage points absolute and sustained for 3 minutes — WARN/ESCALATE

Runbook: quick checklist for running a synthetic canary sweep
- prep: choose route(s), choose model variant(s), choose profile(s). Add ticket link and owner in the canary experiment doc.
- smoke: run baseline-peak at 25% of target for 2 minutes to confirm harness connectivity.
- sweep: run each profile for the configured duration (see matrix below). Collect traces and export to experiment workspace (s3://redwood-experiments/canary-sim/YYYYMMDD).
- evaluation: run automated eval harness for hallucination-probe profile and embedding drift checks.
- decision: owner approves -> continue to real traffic staging; any FAILs -> rollback model variant and open incident.

Default durations and sampling (starter values):
- baseline-peak: 10 minutes
- long-context-sweep: 8 minutes (repeat 3x with different seeds)
- conversational-bursts: 15 minutes (simulate 1k sessions)
- embedding-batch-blast: 5 minutes per batch-size setting (64/128/256)
- hallucination-probe: 12 minutes with batched evals

Data generation notes (implementation tips):
- seed corpus: use curated synthetic knowledge base (no PII). Begin from canned personas + structured templates.
- variability: randomize persona names, dates, small perturbations to tokens to avoid exact replicate detection by caching layers.
- determinism: support a --seed flag so runs can be reproduced exactly when necessary.
- traffic shaping: emulate network jitter and client timeouts to stress retries. Use an HTTP client with configurable latency distribution.

Integrations / scripts (where to find things):
- sim repo: github.com/redwood-inference/canary-sim-scripts (WIP) — contains runner, payload templates, and k6/locust wrappers.
- telemetry: dashboard template in console -> Product -> Canary Simulations (dashboard id: PROD-CAN-SIM-7)
- experiment tracker: Linear issue template RBW-428 (see linked_artifacts above)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we expose synthetic canary runs in the Console UI as a first-class "preflight" action? UX design needed. @Maya to mock.
- What is the canonical authoritative prompt set for hallucination-probe? Need to lock a seed set and version it with the model catalog.
- How to quantify embedding drift into a single alertable metric (threshold vs rolling z-score)? Ops and Applied ML to propose by 2026-03-01.
- Should synthetic runs be billed to customer/orgs when running against Dedicated instances? Legal / Finance guidance required.

Quick commands (examples):
- run baseline peak: python runner.py --route /generate --model redwood-7b-v1 --profile baseline-peak --concurrency 50 --duration 600 --seed 42
- run long context: python runner.py --profile long-context-sweep --context-len 4000 --repeat 3

Postmortem obligations if FAIL observed:
- capture trace ids, sample payloads (sanitized), and export model logs + GPU diagnostics to experiment S3 path
- open incident in Slack #oncall-alerts and create Linear ticket with the label canary-failure
- schedule a 1-hour stewardship call with Product, Applied ML, SRE, and the oncall owner within 24h

Appendix: small example payload template (JSON, sanitized) for long-context-sweep:
{
  "persona": "archaeology-researcher",
  "seed_story": "[synthetic paragraph ~2k tokens about an imaginary dig site]...",
  "query": "Summarize the implications for chronology and list 6 follow-up experiments."
}

Notes to self / timeline:
- 2026-02-01: initial sim runner prototype merged to canary-sim-scripts
- 2026-02-14: this doc initial draft, asking Applied ML for hallucination prompt set by 2026-03-01

References and inspiration:
- internal: rollout-orchestration-workbook-wip.json (cross-ref for gating language)
- external: "Simulating Realistic Loads for Microservices" (notes from infra reading group)

If you're running this: leave a note at the top of the experiment tracker with the exact command used and the seed value so we can reproduce later.
